Thank you both. This is exactly why we have the sign-off protocol, and Evan is raising a critical point that we cannot ignore. Let me lay out where we stand and what needs to happen next.

First, on the ownership reconciliation — Nadia, thank you for completing that work. The 6.4% figure, including the cash-settled positions, is exactly the kind of supporting documentation we need. We should get that spreadsheet attached to the filing package and update the draft accordingly.

But here's the problem: Evan has identified a potential classification issue that goes to the heart of whether a Schedule 13G is even appropriate. If the reporting group actively discussed seeking a board seat with the issuer's largest shareholder, that is not passive-investment conduct. A Schedule 13G requires the reporting person to certify that the securities were acquired in the ordinary course of business and not with the purpose of changing or influencing control of the issuer. Board-seat discussions cut directly against that certification.

So here's what I'm directing as Deputy General Counsel: We are pausing the sign-off process on the Schedule 13G effective immediately. No filing goes out the door until we resolve the classification question. Specifically, I need the following:

1. Evan, please assess whether the board-seat discussion has advanced beyond preliminary exploration. If it has — or if there's a reasonable likelihood it will — we need to reclassify to Schedule 13D and prepare the additional disclosure obligations that come with it, including the purpose statement and related disclosures.

2. Nadia, please attach your ownership reconciliation to the filing package regardless, since we'll need the 6.4% figure and the supporting reconciliation under either filing scenario.

3. I also need compliance to weigh in. Under our filing protocol, I need both securities counsel and compliance sign-offs before I approve anything for submission. Evan has indicated he cannot sign off on the 13G as currently classified, and I'm not going to override that concern.

If reclassification to 13D is warranted, we'll need to revise the purpose section substantially and ensure all 13D disclosure obligations are met. Let's reconvene once Evan has completed his assessment of the board-seat discussions and compliance has had a chance to review. I will not approve this filing for submission until the classification question is resolved and all required sign-offs are in hand.
